___READ_ME___: VS Code / Copilot MCP config. Copy to <your-workspace>/.vscode/mcp.json and
Note the shape differs from Claude Code's: VS Code uses `servers` (not
`mcpServers`) and each entry needs an explicit "type": "stdio".
Keep the args IDENTICAL to .mcp.json. The two files are read by different hosts
and drift silently: on the reference workspace quartz-ctx was given three source
roots in VS Code and one in Claude Code for weeks, so the same tool answered
differently depending on the editor, with no error anywhere.
ALTERNATIVE to listing roots: replace the quartz-ctx --sources-from arg with
--discover . and it will find every crate under the workspace itself —
a Cargo workspace's members and a folder of standalone crates alike.
Never write live counts (nodes, items, communities) into a description string.
They are correct for one day and misleading afterwards - ask the tool instead.
PITFALL - use RELATIVE paths. Both hosts resolve `command` against the workspace
root, so an absolute path works forever on the machine it was written on and
fails for everyone else. The reference workspace shipped an absolute
c:/Users/<someone>/... command in .vscode/mcp.json while .mcp.json used a
relative one - identical behaviour for the author, a dead server for anyone who
copied it. `cortex.sh check-mcp` catches this before a user hits it.
